label: early copy-phase steps (outputs 2-3) of long sequences whose first copied tokens are y/a/n/c/t/f
explanation: 99.6% of activation mass is in the copy phase, at recall_idx 1 (66%, input = the fed-back first original token, prev_tok=<DEL>) and recall_idx 2 (32%). It almost never fires in the original or delimiter phases or after the third output. The fed-back input token is strongly selective: y (39% of mass, 12x lift), then a, n, c, t, f; e/w/l/j almost never. Rate rises with L (absolute t 8-11, to_go 5-7) and falls with more digits in the sequence. The strongest activations (~0.25-0.31) are y as the first token followed by tokens such as 1/c/r/l and later x/m/r/s. The predicate is a necessary context, not a sufficient one: it covers ~88% of activation mass on dev, but only ~5% of matching steps fire. Adding conditions on upcoming outputs (x/r/m/s) raised precision only to ~16% and cut recall, so the remaining selectivity seems to depend on a combination of the stored sequence content that I could not express simply.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=a (+5.82), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+4.60), phase=2 & in_tok=y (+4.03), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+3.94), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+3.52), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+3.37). Lower it: out_tok=b (-4.01), out_tok=m (-3.42), orig_idx=-1 (-3.13), out_tok=3 (-2.95).
